arxiv-1601-06654.title: Nested Artin approximation Thanks: The support from the the project ID-PCE-2011-1023, granted by the Romanian National Authority for Scientific Research, CNCS - UEFISCDI is gratefully acknowledged.
arxiv-1601-06654.creator: Dorin Popescu
arxiv-1601-06654.description: Abstract . A short proof of the linear nested Artin approximation property of the algebraic power series rings is given here. Key words : Henselian rings, Algebraic power series rings, Nested Artin approximation property 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 13B40, Secondary 14B25,13J15, 14B12.

arxiv-1610-07523.title: Seyfert 1 Composite Spectrum using SDSS Legacy Survey Data 2016 Seyfert 1 Composite Spectrum using SDSS Legacy Survey Data – References
arxiv-1610-07523.creator: Nihan Pol, Yogesh Wadadekar
arxiv-1610-07523.description: Abstract We present a rest-frame composite spectrum for Seyfert 1 galaxies using spectra obtained from the DR12 release of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). The spectrum is constructed by combining data from a total of 10,112 galaxies, spanning a redshift range of 0 0 to 0.793 0.793 .

arxiv-1908-00478.title: A Unified Point-Based Framework for 3D Segmentation
arxiv-1908-00478.creator: Hung-Yueh Chiang, Yen-Liang Lin, Yueh-Cheng Liu, Winston H. Hsu
arxiv-1908-00478.description: Abstract 3D point cloud segmentation remains challenging for structureless and textureless regions. We present a new unified point-based framework † † Code is available at https://github.com/ken012git/joint_point_based for 3D point cloud segmentation that effectively optimizes pixel-level features, geometrical structures and global context priors of an entire scene.

arxiv-2105-08896.title: Designing a Pseudo-Random Bit Generator with a Novel 5D-Hyperchaotic System Thanks: The authors are with the LaCIME, Department of Electrical Engineering, École de technologie supérieure, Montreal, QC, Canada, (e-mails: ngoc.nguyen-thi-thu.1@ens.etsmtl.ca, quang-the-toan.bui.1@ens.etsmtl.ca, ghyslai
arxiv-2105-08896.creator: Ngoc T. Nguyen, Toan Q. Bui, Ghyslain Gagnon, Member, IEEE, Pascal Giard, Senior Member, IEEE
arxiv-2105-08896.description: Abstract Dynamic and non-linear systems are emerging as potential candidates for random bit generation. In this context, chaotic systems, which are both dynamic and stochastic, are particularly suitable. This paper introduces a new continuous chaotic system along with its corresponding implementation, which targets field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) .

arxiv-2206-10938.title: Investigating Hadronic Interactions at Ultra-High Energies with the Pierre Auger Observatory
arxiv-2206-10938.creator: Isabel Goos on behalf of the Pierre Auger Collaboration
arxiv-2206-10938.description: Abstract The development of an extensive air shower depends not only on the nature of the primary ultra-high-energy cosmic ray but also on the properties of the hadronic interactions. For energies above those achievable in human-made accelerators, hadronic interactions are only accessible through the studies of extensive air showers, which can be measured at the Pierre Auger Observatory.

arxiv-2210-02297.title: Multiclass Learnability Beyond the PAC Framework: Universal Rates and Partial Concept Classes
arxiv-2210-02297.creator: Alkis Kalavasis, Grigoris Velegkas *, Amin Karbasi
arxiv-2210-02297.description: Abstract In this paper we study the problem of multiclass classification with a bounded number of different labels k k , in the realizable setting. We extend the traditional PAC model to a) distribution-dependent learning rates, and b) learning rates under data-dependent assumptions.

arxiv-2303-09576.title: Phase stability and defect studies of Mg-based Laves phases using defect phase diagrams
arxiv-2303-09576.creator: A. Tehranchi, M. Lipinska-Chwalek, J. Mayer, J. Neugebauer, T. Hickel
arxiv-2303-09576.description: Abstract Laves phases often form as secondary phases in metallic alloys and have a significant effect on their structural properties. Thus, phase stability studies for these chemically and structurally complex phases in addition to mechanical behavior studies are of great interest.

arxiv-2305-00928.title: Breaking the 10 mW/pixel Limit for Kinetic Inductance Detector Readout Electronics
arxiv-2305-00928.creator: Adrian K. Sinclair, James R. Burgoyne, Yaqiong Li, Cody Duell, Scott C. Chapman, Anthony I. Huber, and Ruixuan Xie
arxiv-2305-00928.description: Abstract We demonstrate a prototype kinetic inductance detector (KID) readout system that uses less than 10 mW per pixel. The CCAT-prime RFSoC based readout is capable of reading four independent detector networks of up to 1000 KIDs each. The power dissipation was measured to be less than 40 W while running multi-tone combs on all four channels simultaneously.

arxiv-2310-13786.title: Fundamental Limits of Membership Inference Attacks on Machine Learning Models
arxiv-2310-13786.creator: Eric Aubinais & Elisabeth Gassiat, Pablo Piantanida
arxiv-2310-13786.description: Abstract Membership inference attacks (MIA) can reveal whether a particular data point was part of the training dataset, potentially exposing sensitive information about individuals. This article provides theoretical guarantees by exploring the fundamental statistical limitations associated with MIAs on machine learning models. More precisely, we first derive the statistical quantity that governs the effectiveness and success of such attacks.

arxiv-2505-17874.title: Relationship of structural disorder and stability of supercooled liquid state with glass-forming ability of metallic glasses
arxiv-2505-17874.creator: J.B. Cui, R.A. Konchakov, G.V. Afonin, A.S. Makarov, G.J. Lyu, J.C. Qiao, N.P. Kobelev, V.A. Khonik
arxiv-2505-17874.description: Abstract We performed calorimetric studies of 26 metallic glasses and calculated the excess entropy and excess enthalpy with respect to their counterpart crystals. On this basis, we introduced a dimensionless entropy-based parameter σ s ​ c ​ l \sigma_{scl} , which characterizes structural disordering and stability of the supercooled liquid state upon heating.

arxiv-2506-09522.title: Revisit What You See: Disclose Language Prior in Vision Tokens for Efficient Guided Decoding of LVLMs
arxiv-2506-09522.creator: Beomsik Cho, Jaehyung Kim
arxiv-2506-09522.description: Abstract Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across various multimodal tasks by integrating visual perception with language understanding. However, conventional decoding strategies of LVLMs often fail to successfully utilize visual information, leading to visually ungrounded responses. While various approaches have been proposed to address this limitation, they typically require additional training, multi-step inference procedures, or external model dependencies.

arxiv-2507-08704.title: KG-Attention: Knowledge Graph-Guided Attention at Test-Time via Bidirectional Information Aggregation
arxiv-2507-08704.creator: Songlin Zhai, Guilin Qi, Yuan Meng
arxiv-2507-08704.description: Abstract Knowledge graphs (KGs) play a critical role in enhancing large language models (LLMs) by introducing structured and grounded knowledge into the learning process. However, most existing KG-enhanced approaches rely on parameter-intensive fine-tuning, which risks catastrophic forgetting and degrades the pretrained model’s generalization. Moreover, they exhibit limited adaptability to real-time knowledge updates due to their static integration frameworks.

arxiv-2602-20735.title: RMIT–ADM+S at the MMU-RAG NeurIPS 2025 Competition
arxiv-2602-20735.creator: Kun Ran, Marwah Alaofi, Danula Hettiachchi, Chenglong Ma, Khoi Nguyen Dinh Anh, Khoi Vo Nguyen, Sachin Pathiyan Cherumanal, Lida Rashidi, Falk Scholer, Damiano Spina, Shuoqi Sun, Oleg Zendel
arxiv-2602-20735.description: Abstract This paper presents the award-winning RMIT-ADM+S system for the Text-to-Text track of the NeurIPS 2025 MMU-RAG Competition. We introduce Routing-to-RAG (R2RAG), a research-focused retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture composed of lightweight components that dynamically adapt the retrieval strategy based on inferred query complexity and evidence sufficiency.

pmc-10607114.title: Hypertonic Salt Solution Enhances Inflammatory Responses in Cultured Splenic T-Cells from Dahl Salt-Sensitive Rats but Not Dahl Salt-Resistant Rats
pmc-10607114.creator: Sungmin Jang, Jee Young Kim, Cheong-Wun Kim, Inkyeom Kim, Ha Won Kim
pmc-10607114.description: This study aimed to delineate the effect of sodium chloride on the induction of inflammatory responses and the development of hypertension in Dahl salt-sensitive (SS) and salt-resistant (SR) rats. Splenocytes were isolated from the spleens of SS and SR rats, and cultured on anti-CD3-coated plates for 5 days.

pmc-10612435.title: Evaluation of a mobile-application educational intervention on the knowledge, attitude, and practice of patients in postoperative care for lumbar disk herniation surgery: A randomized control trial
pmc-10612435.creator: Sohaila Sadeghpour Ezbarami, Fatemeh Zarei, Shima Haghani
pmc-10612435.description: Objective:We aimed to evaluate the impact of a mobile-based educational program on patients’ postoperative care for lumbar disk herniation surgery.Methods:A randomized controlled trial was conducted at Fayaz-Bakhsh Hospital, Tehran, Iran. Patients with lumbar disc herniation surgery experience were randomized to the intervention and control groups (learning with the LUmbar CAring Training-app).

pmc-10631069.title: Are the sensorimotor control capabilities of the hands the factors influencing hand function in people with schizophrenia?
pmc-10631069.creator: Yu-Jen Lai, Yu-Chen Lin, Chieh-Hsiang Hsu, Huai-Hsuan Tseng, Chia-Ning Lee, Pai-Chuan Huang, Hsiu-Yun Hsu, Li-Chieh Kuo
pmc-10631069.description: BackgroundPrevious works reported people with schizophrenia experienced inferior hand functions which influence their daily participation and work efficiency. Sensorimotor capability is one of indispensable elements acting in a well-executed feed-forward and feedback control loop to contribute to hand performances. However, rare studies investigated contribution of sensorimotor ability to hand functions for people with schizophrenia.

pmc-10647172.title: Prevalence and risk factors of vitamin D deficiency among patients with chronic myofascial pain syndrome: a cross-sectional study
pmc-10647172.creator: Pimpitcha Channarong, Chanwit Phongamwong
pmc-10647172.description: BackgroundMyofascial pain syndrome (MPS) is a common muscle condition characterized by painful trigger points. Vitamin D deficiency has been recognized as a precipitating factor of MPS. The present study aimed to determine the prevalence and risk factors of vitamin D deficiency in patients with chronic MPS.

pmc-10729786.title: Explainable artificial intelligence for omics data: a systematic mapping study
pmc-10729786.creator: Philipp A Toussaint, Florian Leiser, Scott Thiebes, Matthias Schlesner, Benedikt Brors, Ali Sunyaev
pmc-10729786.description: Researchers increasingly turn to explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to analyze omics data and gain insights into the underlying biological processes. Yet, given the interdisciplinary nature of the field, many findings have only been shared in their respective research community. An overview of XAI for omics data is needed to highlight promising approaches and help detect common issues.

pmc-11312969.title: Reduced Cervical Muscle Fat Infiltrate Is Associated with Self-Reported Recovery from Chronic Idiopathic Neck Pain Over Six Months: A Magnetic Resonance Imaging Longitudinal Cohort Study
pmc-11312969.creator: Suzanne J Snodgrass, Kenneth A Weber, Evert O Wesselink, Peter Stanwell, James M Elliott, Marcus Schiltenwolf
pmc-11312969.description: Background: It is unclear why neck pain persists or resolves, making assessment and management decisions challenging. Muscle composition, particularly muscle fat infiltrate (MFI), is related to neck pain, but it is unknown whether MFI changes with recovery following targeted interventions.

pmc-11577027.title: Soil community history strengthens belowground multitrophic functioning across plant diversity levels in a grassland experiment
pmc-11577027.creator: Angelos Amyntas, Nico Eisenhauer, Stefan Scheu, Bernhard Klarner, Krassimira Ilieva-Makulec, Anna-Maria Madaj, Benoit Gauzens, Jingyi Li, Anton M Potapov, Benjamin Rosenbaum, Leonardo Bassi, Pamela Medina van Berkum, Ulrich Brose
pmc-11577027.description: Biodiversity experiments revealed that plant diversity loss can decrease ecosystem functions across trophic levels. To address why such biodiversity-function relationships strengthen over time, we established experimental mesocosms replicating a gradient in plant species richness across treatments of shared versus non-shared history of (1) the plant community and (2) the soil fauna community.

pmc-11603256.title: BFR2: a curated ribosomal reference dataset for benthic foraminifera
pmc-11603256.creator: Maria Holzmann, Ngoc-Loi Nguyen, Inès Barrenechea Angeles, Jan Pawlowski
pmc-11603256.description: Benthic foraminifera are one of the major groups of marine protists that also occur in freshwater and terrestrial habitats. They are widely used to monitor current and past environmental conditions. Over the last three decades, thousands of DNA sequences have been obtained from benthic foraminiferal isolates.

pmc-12611490.title: Exosomal miRNA-720 as a potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-12611490.creator: Ji Min Kim, Hye Seon Kim, Jin Seoub Kim, Ji Won Han, Soon Kyu Lee, Heechul Nam, Pil Soo Sung, Si Hyun Bae, Jong Young Choi, Seung Kew Yoon, Jeong Won Jang
pmc-12611490.description: Background/AimsCirculating exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs) can serve as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for cancer. This study aimed to identify specific miRNAs in serum exosomes of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and validate their biological functions as novel diagnostic and predictive biomarkers.MethodsSerum exosomal miRNAs in patients with HCC (n = 241) and without HCC (n = 45) were measured by qRT-PCR.

pmc-12618291.title: Laparoscopic enucleation vs. pancreatectomy for small pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms: long-term functional and oncological outcomes
pmc-12618291.creator: Takayuki Miura, Shuichi Aoki, Shimpei Maeda, Masaharu Ishida, Masamichi Mizuma, Kiyoshi Kume, Keigo Murakami, Atsushi Masamune, Toru Furukawa, Takashi Kamei, Michiaki Unno
pmc-12618291.description: BackgroundLaparoscopic surgery is being increasingly used for pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PanNENs). Although laparoscopic regular pancreatectomy (LRP) is frequently performed, laparoscopic enucleation (LE), a parenchyma-sparing technique, may be better in preserving pancreatic endocrine function. However, limited evidence is available regarding the long-term oncological and endocrine outcomes of these two laparoscopic methods.

pmc-12914948.title: Acoustic stimulation and other emerging approaches to enhance sleep: design notes for the next generation of closed-loop neurostimulation technology
pmc-12914948.creator: William G. Coon, Sophie J. Nilsson, Michael T. Smith, Matthew J. Reid
pmc-12914948.description: Sleep is indispensable to human health, supporting memory consolidation, emotional regulation, immune function, and metabolic homeostasis. Despite its importance, chronic sleep disturbances are pervasive, with especially high prevalence in operational and clinical populations. This review synthesizes recent advances in sleep enhancement through closed-loop neurostimulation, focusing on systems that dynamically interact with endogenous brain rhythms to improve sleep quality and efficiency.

pmc-13195223.title: Evaluating an educational supportive care program on functional status and quality of life among women with breast cancer post-mastectomy in Egypt
pmc-13195223.creator: Ftama Kamal Ali, Imad Aljarrah, Rabia Hani Haddad, Soheir Mahmoud Abd El-Hamid, Ashraf Jehad Abuejheisheh
pmc-13195223.description: Background:Women who have undergone mastectomy often report fatigue, shoulder dysfunction, and a diminished quality of life. Structured educational and supportive care programs have the potential to facilitate improved functional recovery and overall well-being post-surgery.Aim:This research aimed to evaluate the effect of the educational supportive care program on fatigue, shoulder functional ability, and quality of life among women after mastectomy.

pmc-13354789.title: Eco-friendly nanocomposite SA/Al2O3/Ag2Mo2O7 microbeads for fast and sustainable photo-induced adsorption of methylene blue dye from industrial wastewater
pmc-13354789.creator: Mohamed A El-Damanhoury, Ahmed H Mangood, Enas M Abou-Taleb, Ahmed M Rashad, Mohamed S Hellal
pmc-13354789.description: The increasing release of hazardous synthetic dye waste poses a serious threat to the environmental and human health. In this study, a novel ternary nanocomposite was designed as an innovative photo-responsive adsorbent by embedding poly silver molybdate (Ag2Mo2O7) and alumina nanoparticles (Al2O3) into a sodium alginate (SA) polymeric matrix.

pmc-13393890.title: Unraveling EFL students’ technology self-efficacy, emotions and behavioral intentions in leveraging large language models: the serial mediation of perceptions and attitudes
pmc-13393890.creator: Zhaoyang Shan, Manman Shan, Lanyun Ding, Yonggang Su
pmc-13393890.description: With the growing momentum to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into education, large language models (LLMs) have shown great potential for English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning. However, the relationships between EFL students’ technology self-efficacy, emotions toward LLM-assisted English learning, and their behavioral intentions remain underexplored.

pmc-13511289.title: Oral GLP‐1RA TERN‐601 for Adults With Obesity/Overweight: Placebo‐Controlled, Multiple‐Ascending‐Dose, Phase 1 and 2 Studies
pmc-13511289.creator: W Timothy Garvey, Julio Rosenstock, Harold E Bays, Douglas Denham, Anita Kohli, Melanie Haines, Christopher Jones, Ellen Kwan, Erin Castelloe, Tonya Marmon, Emil Kuriakose, Cara Nelson

pmc-13608714.title: Research on the Performance Prediction of Fly Ash Slurry by Neural Network Based on Information Bottleneck Theory and Attention Mechanism
pmc-13608714.creator: Botuan Deng, Zifan Li, Yujun Lai, Yixiang Feng, Bin Sun, Ruilin Zhang, Yunwei Bai
pmc-13608714.description: Highlights An IB-AM-CNN model predicts six fly ash slurry properties from three mix proportion variables.Dual optimization cuts mean error from 18.38% to 10.26%, a 44% improvement over baseline CNN.A model-derived recommended mix (1.25:1 w/b ratio, 20% fly ash, 10% water glass) was evaluated through field loading tests.
